newsitem.title: FINLAND: HELSINKI BOURSE SEES NEW REMOTE MEMBERS EARLY 1997.
newsitem.headline: HELSINKI BOURSE SEES NEW REMOTE MEMBERS EARLY 1997.

text.p: The Helsinki Stock Exchange expects to have new remote members early next year, managing director Juhani Erma said on Tuesday.

A law making possible remote membership -- initially planned to be in force at the start of this year -- came into force in August, delaying the process so that the bourse's only remote member so far is Den Danske Bank .
"There will surely be some more during the early part of the year," Erma told Reuters in an interview.
He said it was difficult to estimate how many new members would join next year, but in all there had been interest from over 20 foreign brokerages.

Some of these could have become members sooner, but the delay in legislation had prompted them to list elsewhere first and tight brokerage resources could mean their plans to join Helsinki may be shelved for some time, Erma said.
